Fixtures are 1.5 s, 440 Hz, 44.1 kHz stereo sine waves generated with ffmpeg
(never downloaded). Regenerate with, from this directory:

S="-f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=1.5:sample_rate=44100 -ac 2 -y"
M='-metadata title="Sine Title" -metadata artist="Test Artist" -metadata album="Test Album" -metadata date=2001 -metadata genre=Test'
ffmpeg $S -c:a flac $M -metadata comment=hello -metadata track=3 sine.flac
ffmpeg $S -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 64k $M -metadata track=3/9 sine.mp3
ffmpeg $S -c:a libvorbis -q:a 1 -metadata title="Sine Title" -metadata artist="Test Artist" sine.ogg
ffmpeg $S -c:a aac -b:a 64k sine_aac.m4a
ffmpeg $S -c:a alac sine_alac.m4a

WAV and AIFF test inputs are generated in memory by the tests.

The Opus fixture is the same sine wave, but at 48 kHz - the rate Opus always
runs at - and it carries the same two tags:

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=1.5:sample_rate=48000 -ac 2 -c:a libopus -b:a 96k -metadata title="Sine Title" -metadata artist="Test Artist" sine.opus

The Matroska fixture holds the same encoded stream in a Matroska container,
so the two files decode to the same samples:

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=1.5:sample_rate=48000 -ac 2 -c:a libopus -b:a 96k sine_opus.mkv
